name: Amana / Community of True Inspiration

facts.value: 1714, under Eberhard Ludwig Gruber in Wetterau

citations.excerpt: The Society became attached to the Separatist leader, Eberhard Ludwig Gruber (d. 1728) in Wetterau in 1714

facts.value: Associated with Eberhard Ludwig Gruber from 1714. Christian Metz led the emigration

citations.excerpt: in 1842–1844 about 600 members, led by Christian Metz, the “divine instrument” of the Society, emigrated from Germany to the United States and settled in a colony called Ebenezer
The Society became attached to the Separatist leader, Eberhard Ludwig Gruber (d. 1728) in Wetterau in 1714

facts.value_before_verify: Eberhard Ludwig Gruber. Christian Metz led the emigration

facts.value: Belief in present-day inspiration. Communal property, opposition to war and oaths, and no baptism.

citations.excerpt: formerly the True Inspiration Society (so called from its belief in the present inspiration of the truly godly and perfectly pious)
The Inspirationists are opposed to war and to taking of oaths.

facts.value: A German communal religious society. About 600 members moved to Ebenezer near Buffalo, New York, in 1842-1844 and from 1855 to Amana, Iowa.

citations.excerpt: in 1842–1844 about 600 members, led by Christian Metz, the “divine instrument” of the Society, emigrated from Germany to the United States and settled in a colony called Ebenezer
The township is the home of a German religious communistic society, the Amana Society
in 1855 the colony began to remove to its present home

facts.value_before_verify: A German communal religious society that moved to New York in 1842-1844 and then to Amana, Iowa.
